newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Luxembourg banks merge back office fund activities.
newsitem.headline: Luxembourg banks merge back office fund activities.

text.p: Luxembourg's big four banks have pooled their back office investment fund management operations to create Europe's largest administrator of unit trusts, officials said on Friday.

European Fund Administration SA (EFA) will manage the shareholder registers, accounts and calculation of net asset value of funds issued by Banque Generale de Luxembourg SA, Kredietbank Luxembourgeoise SA, Banque et Caisse d'Epargne de l'Etat (BCEE) and Banque de Luxembourg SA.
"Our objectives are ambitious," KB Luxembourg board member and EFA deputy chairman Jean-Marie Barthel told Reuters.
"EFA will be a profit centre which will be run as an independent company with its own management and staff," he said.
EFA should be fully operational by the end of 1997, after which there will be a two-year transition period while funds are gradually transferred to EFA's administration.
Barthel said the marketing and asset management of funds will remain in the hands of the individual banks. "Existing funds will continue to be commercialised by the banks."
But around the year 2000 it was foreseen that EFA could sell its services to other investment fund issuers in Luxembourg and - under planned new European Union legislation - around Europe.

EFA should help the Luxembourg banks maintain the competitive edge the Grand Duchy has had in investment funds since it was the first European Union country to legislate the sector in 1983, Barthel said.

"The objective is, nationally, to strengthen the role of each bank in the administration of unit trusts...and, internationally, to position ourselves in the European Union to benefit from evolving EU legislation," Barthel said.
He was referring to a proposal to amend the EU's 1985 directive on unit trusts.
EFA was set up by the banks on October 15 with paid-in capital of 100 million Luxembourg francs, out of planned total capitalisation of 250 million.
BGL owns 39 percent of EFA, KB Luxembourg 32 percent, BCEE 17.5 percent and Banque de Luxembourg 11.5 percent, Barthel said.
BGL is a unit of Belgium's biggest bank Generale de Banque SA. KB Luxembourg is a unit of Belgian bank holding company Almanij NV.
